guide.title: Patient Movement & Lifting
guide.lead: The safest lift is the one you plan. Know the weight and the route, get enough people, use the power lift and power grip, and talk on every move. Around helicopters, approach only when the crew signals you, from the front and never from uphill or the tail.

steps.title: Back
steps.text: Straight and locked; bend at the hips and knees.

steps.title: Grip
steps.text: Palms up, whole hand around the handle (power grip), hands about 25 cm apart.

steps.title: Lift
steps.text: Load close; push up with the legs; exhale; pivot, never twist.

steps.title: Talk
steps.text: One leader: "Ready? Lift on three: one, two, three." Same for lowering.

sections.title: Stairs and tight spaces
rows: Patient facing down (feet first); the person at the feet takes much of the weight, the head person controls; tracks if fitted
Scoop, flexible stretcher or a carry sheet with enough people
4–6 or more people, rated equipment, mechanical lifts, fire service early
Stop, secure the patient, call for more help

sections.title: Helicopter landing zone
items: At least 30 × 30 m (100 × 100 feet), firm, as level as possible, clear of wires, poles and loose objects
Mark the corners with lights; tell the crew about wires, slopes and wind
No one approaches until the crew signals
Approach from the front, in the pilot's view – never from the tail or the uphill side
Secure loose items; no running; eye protection

figures.alt: A landing zone with lit corners, wind indicator, a power line marked as a hazard, and the safe approach arc at the front of the helicopter, tail and uphill sides crossed out.

quiz.q: A provider lifts a board bending at the waist, legs straight, fingers-only grip. He's violating:
options: Leg lift, straight back and power grip
Nothing if his back is straight

quiz.q: 90 kg patient in a stair chair down narrow stairs. Most accurate?
options: Patient faces down the stairs; the foot-end rescuer takes much of the weight; both use their legs
quiz.explanation: Use tracks if the chair has them.

quiz.q: At night the wind at your landing zone shifts direction. You:
options: Radio the new wind direction, adjust markings if needed, stay clear on landing
Stand in the middle with a torch
quiz.explanation: Helicopters land into the wind; lights in the pilot's eyes blind them.

quiz.q: 180 kg patient who can't sit must go down narrow stairs. Best?
options: Flexible or bariatric carry device with 4–6 or more rescuers
Palms up, whole hand around the handle
From the front, when signalled, in the pilot's view
Running, as soon as it lands

quiz.q: Minimum landing zone size commonly used:
quiz.explanation: Larger at night or for big aircraft.

quiz.q: Your partner hurts their back halfway down the stairs. You:
options: Stop, secure the patient safely, call for help
quiz.explanation: Two injured providers help no one.

options: One leader counts; lift on the agreed word

flashcards.question: Body mechanics
flashcards.answer: Lift with your legs, back straight, feet shoulder-width apart, load close, pivot don't twist.

flashcards.question: Power lift
flashcards.answer: Squat with a straight back, power grip, load close, push up with the legs, exhale.

flashcards.question: Power grip
flashcards.answer: Palms up, whole hand around the handle, hands about 25 cm apart.

flashcards.question: Stair chair down stairs
flashcards.answer: Patient faces down the stairs; foot-end rescuer takes much of the weight; head-end controls; coordinate each step; tracks if fitted.

flashcards.question: Landing zone
flashcards.answer: At least about 30 × 30 m (100 × 100 feet), firm, level, clear of wires and debris, corners lit. Approach from the front when signalled; never the tail or uphill side.

flashcards.question: Direct vs prepared lifts
flashcards.answer: Raise the stretcher and use transfer devices to reduce bending; lift from the ground only when needed.

flashcards.question: Bariatric moves
flashcards.answer: 4–6 or more rescuers, rated equipment, lifts and transfer mats, plan the route, call for help early.

flashcards.question: Team lifting words
flashcards.answer: One leader: "Ready? Lift on three: one, two, three." Same pattern to lower.

critical.scenario: Third-floor walk-up: 100 kg woman with heart failure, SpO₂ 89%, can't walk. You and your partner are tired; narrow stairs with a turn.
critical.question: Plan?

options.t: Oxygen and position of comfort now, call for more people (fire service), then carry in a stair chair sitting up
Lay her flat on a board

critical.explanation: If she deteriorates, a faster carry device with whoever is there.
critical.kpi: Plans a safe move with adequate resources

critical.scenario: Night landing zone in a sloping field; wind from the north; power line along one fence.
critical.question: Setup and approach?

options.t: Choose the flattest area away from the line, light the corners, tell the crew about the wires, slope and wind; approach only when signalled, from the front and downhill side

critical.kpi: Establishes a safe helicopter landing zone

critical.scenario: Carrying a stable 75 kg man in a stair chair to the lift, your partner feels sharp back pain and can't continue.
critical.question: What do you do?

options.t: Stop, lower and secure the chair, check your partner, call for more help, reassure the patient
Ask the patient to walk the rest
Ask bystanders to lift without guidance

critical.kpi: Responds safely to a crew injury during a move
